mainTopic: The race and then the פייס for תרומת הדשן: why the lottery came, the two תקנות, and which four אמות decided the race
overview: This amud opens the second פרק of יומא. The משנה explains that at first any כהן who wanted to do תרומת הדשן could do it. If many wanted it, they raced up the כבש, and a tie was settled by a finger-count lottery with no thumbs allowed. After one כהן pushed another and broke his leg, the בית דין ruled that the job would only be given out by פייס, the first of four daily lotteries. The גמרא asks why there was no פייס from the start. One answer is that it is a night service, so few were expected to come; the גמרא tests this against אברים ופדרים and against רבי יוחנן's ruling on washing hands. A second version (איכא דאמרי) says the רבנן expected sleep to keep כהנים away, since getting up early is harder than staying up late. The גמרא then asks whether the פייס was really made because of danger, given a ברייתא that bundles the job with סידור מערכה and the two logs. רב אשי answers that there were two separate תקנות. Finally, רב פפא proves that the deciding ארבע אמות are the ones next to the מזבח, and he begins asking whether they include the יסוד and סובב. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The original system: whoever wants it, and a race to break ties
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the earliest practice: any willing כהן did תרומת הדשן. When there were many, they raced up the כבש, and a tie went to a finger lottery run by the ממונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, any כהן who wanted to remove the ashes from the מזבח did so. When many wanted it, they ran up the ramp. Whoever got within four אמות of the top first won the job. If two arrived at the same time, the ממונה told everyone to stick out their fingers for a count.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is describing the original, early method for choosing which כהן would do תרומת הדשן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were three levels. First, if only one כהן wanted the job, he simply did it. If many wanted it, there was a race. If the race ended in a tie, there was a finger-count lottery. The finish line was not the very top of the מזבח but four אמות from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a portion of ashes from the altar, the first service of the day
The ramp leading up to the altar
Four cubits, the winning distance from the top
The appointed כהן in charge of assigning jobs
"Stick out your fingers" (for the lottery count)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse תרומת הדשן with תרומה (the produce gift given to כהנים). Here, לתרום means to lift out ashes from the מזבח.

phrases.english: Initially, whoever wishes
to remove the ashes from the altar removes them.
And when they are many,
they run and go up the ramp.
Whoever gets ahead of his fellow
within four cubits of the top wins the job.
And if both of them were equal (a tie),
the appointed one says to them: Extend your fingers.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה כׇּל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, תרומת הדשן went to any willing כהן. If many wanted it, the winner of a race up the כבש got it. A tie was settled by a finger lottery.

steps.title: Which fingers may be extended for the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The משנה clarifies how the finger-count works: a כהן may extend one or two fingers, but never a thumb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which fingers do they stick out? One or two. But they do not stick out a thumb in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה pauses to explain a technical detail of the finger lottery mentioned just before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lottery worked by counting extended fingers around a circle until reaching a chosen number. A thumb is spread far from the other fingers. So a כהן could stick out a thumb plus a finger to look like two people, and cheat the count. Banning the thumb keeps the lottery honest.

keyTerms.meaning: They extend (put out fingers)
Thumb
The Temple

phrases.english: And what do they extend?
One finger or two.
And they do not extend a thumb in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the mechanics of the הצביעו lottery from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the finger lottery, a כהן extends one or two fingers. Thumbs are not allowed.

steps.title: An injury leads the court to require a lottery
steps.stepSummary: During a tied race, one כהן pushed another, who fell and broke his leg. Seeing the danger, the בית דין ruled that תרומת הדשן would only be assigned by פייס. This was the first of four daily lotteries.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, two כהנים were tied while running up the ramp. One pushed the other, and he fell and broke his leg. When the בית דין saw that this was leading to danger, they made a rule: the ashes would only be removed by lottery. There were four lotteries in the מקדש, and this was the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells the story that ended the race system and replaced it with a mandatory lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the lottery was only used to break a tie. Now it became the only way to choose. The reason for the change is סכנה, physical danger. The משנה also notes that this is the first of four daily פייסות, which sets up the rest of the פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story
Danger
They instituted (made a rabbinic enactment)
A lottery
The court

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the system of four פייסות in the מקדש, which the rest of the פרק goes on to describe.

phrases.english: There was an incident where both of them were equal,
and they were running and going up the ramp,
and one of them pushed his fellow,
and he fell and his leg was broken.
And once the court saw
that they were coming to danger,

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: they instituted that they would not remove the ashes from the altar
except by lottery.
There were four lotteries there,
and this was the first lottery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how the original race system from step 1 was replaced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of danger, בית דין ruled that תרומת הדשן is assigned only by פייס. It is the first of four daily lotteries.
steps.whatToRemember: There were three stages. First, any willing כהן did the job. Then came a race, with a finger lottery for ties. Finally, after an injury, the job was given only by פייס.

steps.title: Why was there no lottery from the beginning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן did not set up a פייס for תרומת הדשן from the start, the way they did for other services.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at the beginning, why didn't the רבנן make a lottery for this job?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a question about the משנה. It sets up the explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other services were given out by lottery. So it seems strange that this one first used a risky race. The גמרא wants to know what the רבנן were thinking at first.

keyTerms.meaning: Originally, at first
What is the reason?
A lottery (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: GEMARA: But originally,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תַּקִּינוּ לַהּ רַבָּנַן פַּיְיסָא?
phrases.english: what is the reason the Sages did not institute a lottery for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תַּקִּינוּ לַהּ רַבָּנַן פַּיְיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the original system in the משנה was a race and not a lottery.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן waited until after an injury to make a פייס for תרומת הדשן.

steps.title: They thought few would come to a night-time job
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that because תרומת הדשן is done at night, the רבנן assumed few כהנים would care to come. Once they saw many came and it led to danger, they made a lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they thought: since it is a night-time job, the כהנים won't consider it important and won't come. Once they saw that the כהנים did come, and that it was leading to danger, they made a lottery for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The רבנן did not expect enough כהנים to compete for a night job to need a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lottery is only needed when many people want the same job. Since this was an עבודת לילה, they expected few volunteers. Reality proved them wrong, and the race became dangerous. So the change was a response to what actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: A service done at night
Not considered important
They thought or assumed

steps.whatToRemember: There was no פייס at first because the רבנן assumed a night service would not attract many כהנים. When many came and it became dangerous, a פייס was instituted.

phrases.english: Originally they thought:
since it is a night service,
it is not important to them, and they won't come.
Once they saw that they do come,
and they come to danger,
they instituted a lottery for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סְבוּר כֵּיוָן דַּעֲבוֹדַת לַיְלָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן assumed a night service would draw few כהנים, so no lottery was needed. Once many came and danger arose, they made one.

steps.title: Limbs and fats are also burned at night, yet they had a lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that night services did not get a פייס. אברים ופדרים are burned at night, and the רבנן still set up a פייס for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the limbs and fats? Burning them is a night service, and the רבנן still set up a lottery for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 5 by pointing to another night service that did get a פייס from the beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said that because תרומת הדשן is done at night, the רבנן assumed few כהנים would come, so no פייס was needed. But burning אברים ופדרים also happens at night, and it did have a פייס. So 'it is at night' cannot be the full reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs of a קרבן עולה, burned on the מזבח
Fats of קרבנות, burned on the מזבח
A service done at night
A lottery (פייס) used to assign Temple jobs

phrases.english: But there are the limbs and the fats,
phrases.notes: Their burning on the altar continues through the night.

phrases.english: which is a nighttime service,
and the Rabbis instituted a lottery for it!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a night service would not get a פייס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: אברים ופדרים are a night service and did get a פייס.

steps.title: Burning limbs and fats is the end of a daytime service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that burning אברים ופדרים is not really a night service. It is the final stage of the daytime קרבן service.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the end of a daytime service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 5 by saying אברים ופדרים are not a true night service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main parts of a קרבן, the שחיטה and the זריקת הדם, happen by day. Burning the limbs and fats at night just finishes that daytime work. So it belongs to the day and is not a real counterexample.

keyTerms.meaning: The end or final stage of a service
Of the daytime

phrases.english: It is the end of a daytime service.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the burning belongs to the day's service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning אברים ופדרים is a night service like תרומת הדשן.
steps.terutzMaskana: It finishes a daytime service, so it is treated as day.

steps.title: Removing the ashes should then count as the start of a daytime service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the same logic around. If late burning counts as day, then תרומת הדשן should count as the beginning of the day's service. It proves this from רבי יוחנן's ruling about washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one too is the start of a daytime service! As רבי יוחנן said: if a כהן washed his hands for תרומת הדשן, the next morning he does not need to wash again, since he already washed at the start of the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that if Step 7 is right, תרומת הדשן should also count as a daytime service. That would undo the answer from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says one קידוש ידים before תרומת הדשן covers the כהן's service after daybreak. The reason he gives is 'he already washed at the start of the service.' That sounds like תרומת הדשן is the opening of the day's service. If so, it is not really a night service, and the reason from Step 5 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning of a service
He washed (sanctified) his hands and feet from the כיור before serving
Removing a portion of ashes from the מזבח
The next day, meaning after daybreak

phrases.aramaic: הַאי נָמֵי תְּחִלַּת עֲבוֹדָה דִימָמָא הִיא,
phrases.english: This too is the start of a daytime service,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he sanctified his hands for the removal of the ashes,
the next day he need not sanctify them again,
because he already sanctified at the start of the service!
phrases.notes: This wording suggests תרומת הדשן is the beginning of the day's service.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי נָמֵי תְּחִלַּת עֲבוֹדָה דִימָמָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of Step 7 against Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 5 that תרומת הדשן is a night service
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Parallel reasoning backed by רבי יוחנן's wording 'מתחילת עבודה', which treats תרומת הדשן as the start of the day.

steps.title: Reread רבי יוחנן: he washed at the outset for service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי יוחנן's words. He did not mean 'the start of the day's service.' He meant 'he already washed at the beginning, for service.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: because he already sanctified his hands at the outset for the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how we read רבי יוחנן's last phrase, so it no longer proves that תרומת הדשן is a daytime service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new reading, רבי יוחנן only says that the earlier washing still works, because the כהן washed for service and did not stop in between. It says nothing about which day תרומת הדשן belongs to. So תרומת הדשן stays a night service, and Step 5 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say' — rereading or correcting the wording of a statement
At the outset, for the service

steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases look almost the same: 'מתחילת עבודה' means 'from the start of the service' (that is, the day's service), while 'מתחילה לעבודה' means 'at the beginning, for service.' The small change in wording removes the proof.

phrases.english: Say: because he already sanctified at the outset for the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by rereading the source it quoted
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the cited statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן treats תרומת הדשן as the beginning of the day's service.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן only says the washing carries over; תרומת הדשן is still a night service.
steps.whatToRemember: First approach: תרומת הדשן had no פייס at first because it is a real night service. אברים ופדרים had a פייס because they finish a daytime service.

steps.title: Another explanation: the רבנן expected sleep to keep כהנים away
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי) explains the original practice differently. The רבנן thought that because of אונס שינה, few כהנים would come. When many came and it became dangerous, they set up a פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: at first the רבנן thought that since people are overcome by sleep, the כהנים would not come. Once they saw that they did come, and it even led to danger, the רבנן set up a lottery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question from Step 4. The reason is not 'night service' but the pull of sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version does not depend on whether תרומת הדשן counts as a night or day service. It depends on the fact that כהנים had to be awake at that hour. The result is the same as in Step 5: the רבנן first expected few volunteers, and when that turned out wrong and led to danger, they made a פייס.

keyTerms.meaning: Originally, at first
Being overcome by sleep
Danger

phrases.english: Some say:
Originally they thought

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא אוֹנֶס שֵׁינָה, לָא אָתוּ.
phrases.english: that since there is the pull of sleep, they would not come.
Once they saw that they did come,
and they were also coming to danger —
the Rabbis instituted a lottery for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of Step 4, in place of Step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why there was no פייס for תרומת הדשן at the start (from Step 4)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן expected אונס שינה to keep כהנים away.

steps.title: Limbs and fats also involve sleep, yet they had a lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second approach with the same example. Burning אברים ופדרים also keeps כהנים from sleep, yet it had a פייס from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the limbs and fats? There too people are pulled by sleep, and the רבנן still set up a lottery for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the איכא דאמרי reason against the same example it used in Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sleep is the reason the רבנן expected few volunteers, the same worry applies to burning אברים ופדרים through the night. Yet that service had a פייס. The answer from Step 7 (end of a daytime service) does not help here, because this approach is about sleep, not about which day the service belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is — introducing a counterexample
They instituted, enacted
The Sages

phrases.english: But there are the limbs and the fats,
where there is the pull of sleep,
and the Rabbis instituted a lottery for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי אֵיבָרִים וּפְדָרִים, דְּאִיכָּא אוֹנֶס שֵׁינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternative reason in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אונס שינה explains why there was no פייס at first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: אברים ופדרים also involve losing sleep and still had a פייס.

steps.title: Staying up late is different from getting up in the middle of the night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that delaying sleep is easier than waking up from it. Burning אברים ופדרים means staying up late, while תרומת הדשן means getting up before dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lying down to sleep is different from getting up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the איכא דאמרי approach by showing that the two services involve different kinds of lost sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן burning אברים ופדרים just goes to bed later, so the רבנן expected plenty of volunteers and set up a פייס. תרומת הדשן requires getting out of bed in the middle of the night, which is much harder, so they expected few volunteers. This closes the second approach.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Lying down to sleep (going to bed late)
From getting up (rising from sleep)

steps.whatToRemember: Second approach (איכא דאמרי): the reason was אונס שינה. אברים ופדרים only mean staying up late, while תרומת הדשן means waking up early, which is much harder.

phrases.english: Lying down to sleep is different from rising.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every service that costs sleep would make the רבנן expect few volunteers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only waking up early (תרומת הדשן) was expected to discourage כהנים; staying up late (אברים ופדרים) was not.

steps.title: Was the lottery really made because of danger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's reason for the פייס. A ברייתא shows that the winner of תרומת הדשן also got סידור מערכה and the two logs. So the פייס seems to exist because of those important tasks, not because of danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: But was the תקנה made for that reason (the danger)? The תקנה was made for this reason! As a ברייתא teaches: whoever won תרומת הדשן also won the arranging of the wood pile and the two logs of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה's story that the פייס was set up because a כהן got hurt. It brings a ברייתא that suggests a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא, the winner of תרומת הדשן also received סידור מערכה and the two logs. Those are valuable jobs that would need a פייס anyway. So the פייס seems to come from the bundled jobs, not from the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: An enactment or rule set up by the חכמים
For that side or reason / for this side or reason
Arranging the wood pile on the מזבח
The two logs of wood placed on the מזבח each morning

phrases.english: But was the enactment for that reason (danger)?
The enactment was for this other reason!
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Whoever won the removal of the ashes
also wins the arranging of the wood pile
and the two logs of wood!
phrases.notes: These tasks are valuable in their own right and would call for a lottery.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַקַּנְתָּא לְהָךְ גִּיסָא הֲוַאי? תַּקַּנְתָּא לְהַאי גִּיסָא הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling why the original practice had no פייס, the גמרא now questions the reason the משנה gives for introducing the פייס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the פייס was made because of the danger incident
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא bundles תרומת הדשן with other important tasks. Those tasks would need a פייס anyway, so danger was not the reason.

steps.title: Two separate enactments, one after the other
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that there were two separate תקנות. First the פייס was made because of danger. Then the חכמים bundled the extra tasks with it so that כהנים would still come to the lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: there were two enactments. At first they thought the כהנים would not come. When they saw that they did come, and that it was even leading to danger, they set up a פייס. Once the פייס was set up, the כהנים stopped coming. They said, 'Who says the lottery will fall to us?' So the חכמים then enacted that whoever won תרומת הדשן would also win סידור מערכה and the two logs, so that the כהנים would come and join the lottery.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. Both reasons are true; they belong to two different תקנות made at different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תקנה, the פייס, came because of danger, just as the משנה says. That created a new problem: כהנים stopped showing up for a lottery they would probably lose. The second תקנה bundled valuable tasks with תרומת הדשן so the prize was worth getting up early for.

keyTerms.meaning: Two separate enactments
A lottery used to assign Temple tasks
Danger
Who says it will fall to us?
So that they will come and join the lottery

steps.whatToRemember: There were two תקנות: (1) the פייס, because of danger; (2) bundling סידור מערכה and the two logs with תרומת הדשן, so כהנים would still come to the פייס.
steps.confusionAlert: The bundled tasks did not cause the פייס. They were added afterward, to fix the low turnout that the פייס itself caused.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
There were two enactments.
At first they thought the priests would not come.
Once they saw that they did come
and were even coming to danger,
they set up a lottery for it.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּתַקִּינוּ לַהּ פַּיְיסָא — לָא אֲתוֹ,
phrases.english: Once they set up the lottery, the priests did not come.
They said: Who says it will fall to us?
So they then enacted for them
that whoever won the removal of the ashes
would also win the arranging of the wood pile
and the two logs of wood,
so that they would come and join the lottery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁתֵּי תַּקָּנוֹת הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 by separating the two reasons into two enactments made at different times.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chronological split: two separate תקנות, each with its own reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one reason could explain the פייס: either danger or the valuable bundled tasks.
steps.terutzMaskana: Danger caused the פייס. The bundling came later, to bring the כהנים back to the פייס.

steps.title: Which four אמות? Ruling out the ground and the bottom of the ramp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the race when many כהנים came. רב פפא begins to work out which ארבע אמות the משנה means. He rules out the ground beside the ramp and the first four אמות of the ramp.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And when they were many, etc.' רב פפא said: It is obvious to me that it is not four אמות on the ground, because we learned 'they run and go up on the ramp.' It is also not the first four אמות of the ramp, because we learned 'they run and go up on the ramp,' and only afterward 'whoever gets ahead of his fellow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה: the race up the כבש. רב פפא starts narrowing down where the deciding ארבע אמות are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כהנים run up the ramp, so the deciding area cannot be on the ground. The משנה mentions 'whoever gets ahead' only after they are already going up. So the contest is decided somewhere higher on the ramp, not in its first four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious to me
Four cubits; the zone that decides who wins
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
The first ones (the first four אמות of the ramp)

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'And when they are many, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה that introduces the new discussion.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me
that it is not four cubits on the ground,
because we learned: 'they run and go up on the ramp.'
It is also not the first four cubits of the ramp,
because we learned: 'they run and go up on the ramp,'
and only afterward: 'whoever gets ahead of his fellow.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְרוּבִּין וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פְּשִׁיטָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section: the גמרא returns to explain another line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deciding ארבע אמות are neither on the ground nor at the bottom of the ramp.

steps.title: The four אמות are the ones next to the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules out four אמות in the middle of the ramp, because the משנה gives no way to know which ones. So the deciding ארבע אמות must be the ones next to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also not four אמות somewhere in the middle, because then the matter would not be defined. It is obvious to me that we learned it about the four אמות next to the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his elimination and reaches his conclusion: the race is decided at the four אמות right by the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A middle section of the ramp has no clear marker, so the משנה could not be relying on it. With the ground, the bottom, and the middle ruled out, only the top remains. The top is the four אמות next to the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: In between; somewhere in the middle
The matter is not defined or clear
Next to the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: In the race up the כבש, the winner is the first כהן to reach the four אמות next to the מזבח.

phrases.english: It is also not four cubits in the middle,
because then the matter would not be defined.
It is obvious to me that we learned it about the area next to the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's elimination from step 15 and states his conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's ארבע אמות are the four אמות of the ramp next to the מזבח.

steps.title: Do the base and ledge count in the four אמות?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the four אמות next to the מזבח include the one-אמה יסוד and the one-אמה סובב, which lie under the top of the ramp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: The four אמות that the חכמים spoke about, are they counted together with the אמה of the יסוד and the אמה of the סובב?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a follow-up question about how to measure the four אמות next to the מזבח. This is only the first half of his question. The other side of the question, and the discussion of it, continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 decided that the race was won in the four אמות next to the מזבח. The ramp's top section runs over the יסוד and the סובב, which are each one אמה wide. So רב פפא asks whether those two אמות count as part of the four. If they do, only two more אמות of ramp are added. If they don't, the four אמות begin farther out.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked / raised a question he did not yet know the answer to
The four אמות that the חכמים mentioned in the משנה
The one-אמה-wide base step at the bottom of the מזבח
The one-אמה-wide ledge that runs around the מזבח higher up
Together with / including

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the יסוד and סובב are separate from the ramp's path. The ramp extends over them as it reaches the top of the מזבח. That is exactly why רב פפא asks whether they count.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
phrases.notes: An open question (a בעיא), not an attack on anything.

phrases.english: The four cubits that they mentioned,
phrases.notes: The four אמות next to the מזבח, as established in Step 16.

phrases.english: are they including the cubit of the base and the cubit of the ledge,
phrases.notes: The ramp overlaps these two cubits. The other side of the question comes right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב פפא's conclusion in Step 16 by asking exactly how the four אמות next to the מזבח are measured.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the four אמות next to the מזבח include the one-אמה יסוד and the one-אמה סובב that lie beneath the ramp.
